sections.theory:
… performance can be increased by applying the laws of motion.

Round Service

The shoulder will be towards the net and the face towards the side line. The feet will be parallel to the service line. Bending the front slightly, hit the ball while tossing it in the air. The first and second laws of motion will apply.

Smash Service

The player, from behind the service line, tossing the ball in the air inside the service area, taking a few steps towards the net and jumping, will hit the ball in the manner of a smash. In this activity the third law of force and the state of balance will apply, because to jump the player will apply force on the surface of the ground with the legs. As a result of the reaction, the body of the player will go up into the air to the same height.

Lifting the ball and biomechanical principles (Digging)

To lift the ball of the service, the fingers of both hands are joined to each other; the thumbs should be together and parallel. Lengthen the arms; as soon as the ball comes near, bending the body forward, lift the ball on the arms in such a way that the ball comes over the head of the booster.

Remember, if the service has been done in the smash way, then the speed of the ball is very fast. According to the second law of motion, material bodies want to maintain their state of rest or motion. Therefore under the law of inertia, to reduce the resistance of the ball to change in motion, as soon as the ball strikes the hands they should be moved backwards …

سروس کا بال اٹھانے کے لیے دونوں ہاتھوں کی انگلیاں آپس میں ملائی جاتی ہیں انگوٹھے اکٹھے اور متوازی ہوں۔ چاہئیں۔ بازوؤں کو لمبا کریں جونہی بال نزدیک آئے جسم کو آگے جھکاتے ہوئے بازوؤں پر بال کو اس طرح اٹھائیں کہ بال بوسٹر کے سر پر آ جائے۔

یاد رکھیں سروس اگر سمیش طریقے سے کی گئی ہو تو بال کی رفتار بہت تیز ہوتی ہے۔ حرکت کے دوسرے قانون کے مطابق مادی اجسام اپنی حالتِ سکون یا حرکت کو برقرار رکھنا چاہتے ہیں۔ لہٰذا جمود کے قانون کے تحت بال حرکت میں تبدیلی کی مزاحمت کو کم کرنے کے لیے جیسے ہی بال ہاتھوں سے ٹکرائے تو انھیں پیچھے کی جانب حرکت …
